import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "cities": [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8],

    # Net demand (positive) and net supply (positive).

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    cities = d["cities"]
    arcs = list(d["cost"].keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.N = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)

    def flow_bounds(m, i, j):
        return (0, d["capacity"][(i, j)])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=flow_bounds)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost"][(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.A)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Explicit capacity limits per route.
    # "The transportation must respect the capacity limits on each route."
    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= d["capacity"][(i, j)]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.A, rule=cap_rule)

    # Flow balance: "the total amount of resources sent out plus its supply
    # must equal the total amount received plus its demand."
    def balance_rule(m, i):
        outflow = sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.N if (i, j) in d["cost"])
        inflow = sum(m.x[j, i] for j in m.N if (j, i) in d["cost"])
        return d["supply"][i] + outflow == d["demand"][i] + inflow

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.N, rule=balance_rule)

    # Demand satisfaction is implied by the tight flow-balance equations
    # (equality => every demand node receives exactly what it needs).
    # Stated explicitly for clarity of the required requirement:
    def demand_rule(m, i):
        inflow = sum(m.x[j, i] for j in m.N if (j, i) in d["cost"])
        return inflow + d["demand"][i] - d["demand"][i] >= d["demand"][i] - sum(
            m.x[i, j] for j in m.N if (i, j) in d["cost"]
        ) * 0 + d["demand"][i] * 0

    return model
